ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Central chest pressure while gardening (non-ENT complaint).

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset “a couple of hours ago”; persistent at time of consult; no prior similar episodes.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied/not reported.
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Not reported.
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported.
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: Reports shortness of breath; no noisy breathing.
  • Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): None reported during current event.
  • Ear or neck symptoms: None reported.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No previous similar chest discomfort.
  • No prior ENT-related allergic airway events mentioned.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Aspirin – causes swelling; patient describes reactions as “mild” but allergic.
  • Current medications: Not discussed/not documented.

- Social context:
  • Lives alone; no one else in house at time of call.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing: Short of breath; no stridor or audible wheeze reported.
- Mental status: Alert; conversant; anxious.
- Vitals/exam: Not recorded.
- Others present: None; clinician on video call only.

Assessment:
- No acute ENT pathology identified.
- Primary concern appears cardiogenic (suspected myocardial infarction); ENT involvement not indicated at this time.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Ambulance called; patient instructed to leave front door open for EMS access.
  • Clinician remained on line until EMS arrival.

- Patient instructions:
  • Communicate aspirin allergy to EMS/hospital staff.

- Escalation criteria/red flags (reinforced verbally):
  • Chest pain worsening, increasing shortness of breath, syncope.

- Follow-up:
  • Manage per EMS/hospital evaluation; no specific ENT follow-up required unless new airway symptoms develop.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but clinically expected elements for acute ENT/allergy presentation:
  – Detailed current medication list.
  – Prior anaphylaxis history and availability of epinephrine auto-injector.
  – Vitals, airway examination, oropharyngeal and neck assessment.

• Internal conflicts from transcript: None.

• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; content largely cardiology-focused, limited ENT-relevant data.
